record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. AISII presents itself as an AI safety institute under KORIKA.

related_bodies.name: AI Safety Institute Indonesia (AISII)
related_bodies.role: It is an initiative of KORIKA, an independent membership association (perkumpulan); no government mandate was found.

related_bodies.name: Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs (Komdigi)
related_bodies.role: It leads AI policy. In May 2026 it completed inter-ministerial discussion of the draft presidential regulations on an AI roadmap and AI ethics, before their submission to the President.

English searches for a national AI safety, security or evaluation institute, commitment, proposal or study. The English search confirms AISII under KORIKA. KORIKA's January 2025 search result also reports proposing a national AI body / AI Safety Institute to the deputy minister, but the page failed direct retrieval and one fallback text copy; only the search excerpt was read and this is a non-government proposal, not a verified government commitment. Government designation remains unresolved. Partial check only; the last full-check date is unchanged.

Read KORIKA's report of its first members' meeting of 2026 (30 April 2026) for KORIKA's legal form; the AISII role now names it as an independent membership association. Partial check; the last full-check date is unchanged.

News search from 17 October 2026 in English and Indonesian, with the communications and digital ministry's press release listing (entries shown with relative times only, so the newest publication date was not verified). Left for review: a release of 23 October republished by Suar naming AISII among the participants in Project NUSA, launched by KORIKA and AI Singapore, and a CNBC Indonesia interview of 30 October in which the ministry's AI director said the national AI roadmap 2026 to 2029 and the AI ethics presidential regulation were still awaiting signature. The ministry's article with the national cyber agency on AI-agent threats could not be read, and the original NUSA release was not found. Partial check, not a full record re-check.

check.language_note: The recorded id query uses a national or official language selected for this country-specific check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. English queries were also run on 17 October 2026; the previously recorded national or official-language coverage and its limits are unchanged.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: The ministry roadmap account does not independently corroborate AISII's institutional status or government designation. KORIKA's own AISII account alone is insufficient independent institutional corroboration. Confidence was low under that rule; none_identified is a bounded search finding, not proof of absence.
check.governance_note: The ministry describes an inter-ministerial committee discussing the draft presidential AI-roadmap regulation, alongside a separate AI ethics regulation. This is primary evidence of the government's policy process, not an institute designation. The separately named AISII is under KORIKA; government assignment was not established. In May 2026 the ministry completed inter-ministerial discussion of both drafts before their submission to the President; its account names no institute or evaluation body.

record.notes:
In September 2026 a member of the steering committee of the research agency BRIN proposed a government AI Safety Institute for testing AI systems; this is an individual proposal, not a government plan.

Komdigi's release on a meeting with a UC Berkeley academic has a Singapore dateline of 28 May 2025 and a publication date of 30 May 2025 in both its header and footer. It says the ministry will explore an AI Safety Institute Network, described as an international network, or an AI laboratory in Indonesia with no stated model-evaluation remit. This is not a government study of a qualifying national institute. AI Safety Institute Indonesia's (AISII) government designation also remains unverified; the status 'None identified' is retained with medium confidence in the recorded evidence.

next_check.reason: Check whether the presidential regulations on the AI roadmap and AI ethics are signed and whether they create or assign a body to evaluate advanced models; check for a government response to the BRIN proposal or a government mandate for AISII.

closest_body.name: AI Safety Institute Indonesia (AISII)
closest_body.note: AISII presents itself as an AI safety institute under KORIKA. Its website describes evaluating AI behaviour in Indonesian and local languages and work on bias, hallucination and misalignment risks. Government assignment remains unverified.
